tasks.title: Implement gated_advance.advance_with_gates FSM gating coordinator
acceptance_criteria: ngv2/gated_advance.py defines advance_with_gates(session_id, db, run_gates, advance, build_evidence) -> dict
build_evidence is called to assemble the gate evidence payload before any gating
run_gates is invoked with the four gates poc_authenticity, sink_presence, sink_reachability, detonation_evidence
advance is invoked exactly once only when all four gates pass
When any gate fails or raises, advance is NOT called and the result dict marks the transition blocked (fail-closed)
No existing committed module is edited; session_api.py and session_gate.py are untouched; all external seams are injected parameters

spec.objective: Create ngv2/gated_advance.py exposing advance_with_gates, which coordinates the four NobleGreed validation gates via an injected run_gates and performs the FSM transition via an injected advance only when every gate passes, failing closed otherwise.
functional_requirements: build_evidence(session_id, db) is invoked to assemble the evidence payload that feeds the gates, before any gate runs.
run_gates is invoked with the assembled evidence and the four gate identifiers poc_authenticity, sink_presence, sink_reachability, detonation_evidence.
When run_gates reports all four gates passing, advance(session_id, db) is invoked exactly once to perform the state transition.
When run_gates reports any gate failing, advance is NOT invoked and the returned dict marks the transition as blocked with the failing gate reasons (fail-closed).
If run_gates or build_evidence raises an exception, the function fails closed: advance is not called and the error is surfaced in the returned dict rather than propagating an uncaught transition.
The returned dict aggregates per-gate pass/fail results together with the advance outcome (when advanced) or the block reason (when blocked).
All external seams (db, run_gates, advance, build_evidence) are consumed only through injected parameters; the module does not import or call session_api/gate_executor/live-db at runtime.
spec.interfaces: def advance_with_gates(session_id: str, db: Any, run_gates: Callable, advance: Callable, build_evidence: Callable) -> dict
edge_cases: build_evidence returns None or an empty payload -> gates run on empty evidence and the result fails closed (no advance).
run_gates raises -> caught, advance not called, error recorded in result dict.
advance raises after all gates pass -> error surfaced in the returned dict, not silently swallowed, and not retried.
run_gates returns results for fewer than four gates -> treated as a fail-closed (missing gate == not passed).
run_gates returns extra/unknown gate keys -> ignored for the pass decision which is keyed on the four required gates.
non_goals: Do not edit session_api.py, session_gate.py, gate_executor.py or any other committed module.
Do not open a live database connection or make network calls; db is an opaque injected handle.
Do not contact external services or auto-submit to huntr.
spec.implementation_notes:
Keep the module dependency-free except for typing. Define the ordered tuple of required gate ids as a module constant. The pass decision must be conjunction over exactly the four required gate ids being present AND passing in the run_gates result. Wrap build_evidence/run_gates/advance calls so any exception converts to a structured blocked/error result. Return shape suggestion: {"advanced": bool, "gates": <run_gates result>, "transition": <advance result or None>, "blocked_reason": <str or None>}.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Fake run_gates returning configurable per-gate pass/fail dicts; fake build_evidence returning a fixed evidence payload; spy advance recording call count and args; an opaque sentinel db object. No real database or network.

token_budget_ratio.note: Logic is small but the fail-closed branch matrix needs thorough coverage.

spec.objective: Create ngv2/session_get_task.py exposing get_task, which extracts the task payload (phase input, target, prior findings, parked package) from a database session row dict and fails closed when a required key is missing.
functional_requirements: get_task returns the phase input value extracted from session_row.
get_task returns the target value extracted from session_row.
get_task returns the prior findings value extracted from session_row.
get_task returns the parked package value extracted from session_row.
When any required key is absent from session_row, get_task fails closed by raising (e.g. KeyError/ValueError) rather than substituting a default.
edge_cases: session_row is an empty dict -> raises (fail-closed) rather than returning empty fields.
A required key is missing while others present -> raises naming the missing key.
session_row contains extra unrelated keys -> ignored, only the four required fields are returned.
Values are nested structures (lists/dicts) -> returned by reference/preserved without mutation.
non_goals: Do not open a live database connection or perform any network/DB I/O; the row is supplied as a plain dict.
Do not edit session_db.py, session_api.py or any committed module.
Do not auto-submit to huntr or contact external services.

Return a new dict mapping the canonical task field names to the extracted values; do not deep-copy nested values.
